summary.intent: Cache one shared, preloaded `SSLContext` for `verify=True` HTTPS requests so `load_verify_locations()` runs once per process instead of once per request, restoring concurrent-request throughput that OpenSSL's slow CA-bundle reload was costing.
summary.issue_fit: Met for the performance mechanism (one cached context avoids a repeated `load_verify_locations()` call) and the `verify=True`/`False` correctness invariants review comments demanded; the PR's informal badssl timing comparison is not independently verifiable offline.
summary.coverage: The single changed file (src/requests/adapters.py) was read in full; merge-base and head behavior of `cert_verify`, `_urllib3_request_context`, and the new module-level preload were traced and diffed; the focused TLS/cert-bundle test selection ran at the reviewed head.
check_details: Reviewer ran the focused TLS/cert-bundle test selection (`tests/test_requests.py -k "pyopenssl_redirect or invalid_ca_certificate_path or invalid_ssl_certificate_files or env_cert_bundles or http_with_certificate or certificate_failure or different_connection_pool_for_tls or different_connection_pool_for_mtls"`) at the reviewed head: 14 passed, 3 failed; all 3 failures reproduce a pre-existing TLS-fixture/OpenSSL mismatch on code paths this diff does not touch.

Reviewer reproduced an import-time crash by patching `certifi.where()` to a missing path and importing `requests` at the reviewed head, then confirmed by reading the merge-base file that the same monkeypatch cannot fail import there.

findings.title: Don't let a missing CA bundle crash `import requests`
findings.trigger: `adapters.py:75-78` builds `_preloaded_ssl_context` from `DEFAULT_CA_BUNDLE_PATH` unconditionally at module import. Patching `certifi.where()` to a missing path and running `import requests` reproduces an immediate `FileNotFoundError`.
findings.impact: Every `import requests` now fails whenever the default CA bundle is missing or unreadable — even for callers who never verify TLS. At the merge-base the same lookup ran only inside `cert_verify()`, so it fired solely for a verified HTTPS request and raised a controlled `OSError` there instead.
findings.change: Build `_preloaded_ssl_context` lazily on first `verify=True` use, or wrap its construction in the same failure handling `cert_verify()` applied, so a broken default bundle fails only a verified request, not `import requests` itself.

observations.fact: `_urllib3_request_context`'s new `os.path.isdir(verify)` check duplicates the `os.path.isdir(cert_loc)` check `cert_verify()` still performs for the same path, exactly as the PR author notes in the PR body.

A third local test, `test_different_connection_pool_for_mtls_settings`, also fails beyond the two failures the run policy names, but its failing assertion exercises the unchanged `verify=False`/mutual-TLS code path, byte-identical at base and head, so it is unrelated to this diff.
observations.evidence: pytest run of `tests/test_requests.py::TestPreparingURLs::test_different_connection_pool_for_mtls_settings` at the reviewed head; `git show 8dd3b26bf59808de24fd654699f592abf6de581e:src/requests/adapters.py`.

requirements.evidence: adapters.py:75-78 and the `elif verify is True: pool_kwargs["ssl_context"] = _preloaded_ssl_context` branch reuse one module-level SSLContext instead of calling `load_verify_locations()` per connection, which is what `conn.ca_certs` previously triggered inside `cert_verify()`.

requirements.evidence: `cert_verify()` only sets `conn.ca_certs`/`conn.ca_cert_dir` when `verify is not True`.
